mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport issuing authority of applicant's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter and AML compliance warranty issued by applicant's licensed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant's licensed commercial bank or financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn declaration of UBO, source of wealth, and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or licensed company service provider in Samoa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: In-country notarization (no apostille required where sworn before Samoan notary)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and certificate of incumbency if a corporate shareholder or director is a non-Samoan entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original jurisdiction's company registry or corporate agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit's consolidated list, United Nations Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic Samoa sanctions orders. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, trigger enhanced due diligence measures under the AML/CFT Act 2018, including source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Services Centre (SIFSC) online company registration portal (administered by MCIL – Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official language of incorporation. Any non-English name must be romanized or transliterated strictly into Latin script, and no characters outside the English alphabet are permitted in the registered corporate name. The name must appear in exact English form on all external correspondence and certificates.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice issued by the Registrar of International Companies, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar within 14 days, stating the grounds for reversal and attaching evidence of prior ministerial approval for any sensitive token. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may petition the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review within 21 days of the decision. A name reservation may be extended once by application to the Registrar prior to expiry, for an additional 30-day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where a physical, fully staffed registered office is maintained at the office of the licensed international company service provider in Samoa. A pure virtual office with no physical presence is not acceptable for a licensed venture capital general partner entity, which must demonstrate real management and control within the jurisdiction to satisfy substance requirements and obtain the required financial services license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection in the first year of operation, increasing to 60% where the entity holds a financial services license and maintains outsourced administrative functions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_locality_requirement: The registered office must be situated at a physical street address supplied by a licensed Samoan registered agent; a post office box alone is insufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.director_and_secretary_substance: At least one director, one shareholder, and one secretary may be non-residents of Samoa, but the licensed registered agent must be physically present in Samoa. The venture capital general partner must maintain a local resident agent and, for licensing purposes, a local compliance officer.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.regulatory_license_reference: Venture capital general partner activity qualifies under ISIC 6499 as a financial services business, requiring a Samoa International Financial Services Centre license and prior approval from the Financial Regulator prior to issuance of the certificate of incorporation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1988 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 7–15, 28–30 and Schedule 2; International Companies Regulations 2008, regs. 4–9.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Companies and Trusts Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an International Company (Form IC-1) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; at least one ordinary share must be subscribed; share capital may be expressed in any foreign currency and is not required to be deposited into an escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that: (1) the subscribers set out in the memorandum hereby subscribe to the initial ordinary shares, the first directors accept their appointment, and the share register is opened; (2) the registered office of the Company is fixed at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and the registered agent is appointed to maintain statutory registers; (3) the directors elect a Chairman and appoint a Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, who may open bank accounts, execute capital call notices and sign fund administration documents; (4) the Chairman is authorized to finalize all incorporation filings and pay the registration fee; and (5) all actions taken by officers to carry these resolutions into effect are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL (online portal accessed through a licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request to the Registry through a licensed registered agent. Ensure the proposed name ends with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' and does not conflict with an existing registered name. A reserved name is held for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incumbency of proposed directors (if not already on file)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried due to similarity, file an alternative name or provide a written consent from the prior holder within 14 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, via licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form IC-1, execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association, obtain signed declarations of compliance from subscribers and directors, and file the application together with the prescribed registration fee through the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the application for defective witnessing or missing particulars, correct the defects and resubmit the application within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, files the Memorandum and Articles, and opens the public register entry. The Company thereafter prepares its share certificates and opens its statutory share register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains typographical errors, apply for reissuance through the registered agent on Form IC-1A; no fee is imposed within 5 business days if the error is attributable to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Governance Induction
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolutions, record share subscriptions, issue share certificates, confirm officer appointments, and open the statutory registers, including the register of members, register of directors and register of charges.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any procedural defect in the minutes is identified, adopt a ratifying resolution at the next board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Regulatory Notification and AML/CFT Program Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (IFSA) in coordination with the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify IFSA that the Company intends to operate as the general partner of a venture capital fund, appoint a compliance officer, and submit an initial anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing (AML/CFT) program before commencing any fund management activities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IFSA raises questions, submit a remediation plan within 15 business days describing corrective measures and enhanced monitoring.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (IFSA), Ministry of Finance, Government of Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Category B – International Financial Services Provider Licence (Fund Manager / Venture Capital General Partner)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category 3) – office-based financial services, no industrial installation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions from ordinary operations; sanitary effluent discharged to public sewer where available; solid waste collection by licensed carriers under the Waste Management Regulations 1990 and the Environmental Pollution Control Act 2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority; building occupancy permit from the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA); workplace registration under the Labour and Employment Act 2013 with the Ministry of Labour; electrical wiring certificate issued by applicable government inspector.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa; official portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws (e-filing through the Digital Revenue System on the TaXChange platform)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporation of the International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 2008 must be effected through a licensed sponsor/registered agent of the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA). After incorporation, apply to the Commissioner of the Ministry for Revenue for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) using Form TIN-01, submitting the certificate of incorporation, registered office certificate, agent consent, and know-your-customer documentation. Thereafter, file the annual declaration with SIFA (not an income tax return) and obtain the Certificate of Exemption from Taxes under Section 111 of the International Companies Act 2008; the exemption certificate confirms that no Samoa income tax or VAGST applies to offshore business activities and that the IC is outside the domestic tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election. An IC's exempt status is mandatory rather than elective; a licensed IC engaging in business with Samoan residents or deriving Samoa-source income without an approved waiver automatically becomes taxable on that income under the Income Tax Act 2012 and the VAGST Act 2003. The functional election is the statutory conversion between IC form (tax-exempt offshore) and domestic company form (fully taxable), permitted by the International Companies Act 2008.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 120,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; an IC supplying services exclusively to non-residents is outside the VAGST net and may still voluntarily register to claim input credits against zero-rated export supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or digital signature mandate exists in Samoa. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue standard tax invoices showing the supplier TIN and VAGST registration number, and file periodic returns electronically through the MfR Digital Revenue System.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under the VAGST Act 2003 to exports of goods removed from Samoa and to exported services supplied to a non-resident recipient for benefit wholly outside Samoa. A Venture Capital General Partner may therefore zero-rate management fees, carried-interest structuring, advisory, and administrative services supplied to an offshore fund for non-resident limited partners; the IC tax exemption certificate independently removes VAGST regardless of registration status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (preliminary customs bill of entry)
Bill of Lading or Master Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing FX repatriation through a licensed bank
Commercial invoice together with the executed offshore fund and GP services agreement identifying the non-resident recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner may reassess within 4 years, extended to 7 years for fraud or wilful misrepresentation. Invalid zero-rating triggers VAGST at 15% on the full consideration, late-payment penalties of 2% per month, and a shortfall penalty up to 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion or intentional misstatement. Criminal exposure includes fines up to WST 20,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years per offence under the VAGST Act 2003 and the Tax Administration Act 2012; input tax credits are retrospectively clawed back with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, acting as the monetary authority and foreign exchange regulator under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1979 (as amended). CBS exercises delegated control through licensed Authorized Dealers, which are all CBS-licensed commercial banks. The Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) separately regulates the International Company registry and the registered agent network, but has no foreign exchange competence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoa tala (WST) is subject to a managed float with periodic CBS intervention; the currency is not freely convertible offshore, and the domestic interbank market is thin. Current-account transactions, including profit remittances, dividend distributions, management fees, and service payments, are processed freely by Authorized Dealers upon submission of bona fide documentary evidence. Capital-account transactions, including inward equity investment, loan injections, capital repayments, and portfolio transfers, require prior CBS authorization or an Authorized Dealer exercise of delegated authority, with full disclosure of the beneficial owner. For International Companies (ICs) designated as non-resident, foreign-currency accounts are permitted and remittances to non-resident investors are treated as current-account flows if supported by audited financial statements, board resolutions, and the relevant exchange-control declaration. Profit remittance is structurally unimpeded for a tax-exempt IC, but the practical hurdle is the banks' insistence on proving the underlying fund economics and the absence of a 'shell' purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulations 1979, resident exporters must receive full payment for exported goods within six months of the date of exportation and must surrender any foreign-currency export proceeds to an Authorized Dealer within 30 days of receipt, with the statutory default being 100% conversion of qualifying export receipts into WST. General exemptions exist for certain service exporters, reinvoicing centers, and entities granted non-resident status. An International Company acting as a Venture Capital GP has no local physical export proceeds; management fees and carried-interest receipts from non-resident fund investors are classified as invisible earnings and are outside the surrender rule, provided the IC maintains its non-resident designation and files the applicable CBS balance-of-payments statistical returns through its Authorized Dealer.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (USD/WST) plus Multi-currency Operational Account for MT103 settlement
Operational Account / Cross-border settlement rail (SWIFT and correspondent banking)
Operational Account (USD or WST) for domestic treasury needs
General Purpose Operational Account; non-resident offshore structures frequently declined

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW — structurally constrained. Samoa has no fintech EMI or digital-bank licensing category; the CBS recognizes only licensed banks as Authorized Dealers and no foreign EMI authorization confers clearing or settlement privileges in Samoa. An offshore EMI cannot act as the primary treasury rail for the IC because Samoan Authorized Dealers will reject funding and receipt flows through an unlicensed third-country payment institution absent a correspondent banking relationship, and the IC's own AML/KYC stack must ultimately sit inside a CBS-licensed institution. EMIs are acceptable only as a supplementary pass-through for LP bridge payments if the EMI maintains a pooled settlement account with a CBS-licensed correspondent and the IC preserves a direct SWIFT MT103 audit trail; in practice this elevates false-positive sanctions hits and adds settlement delay.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is strongly preferred and in practice effectively mandatory. CBS-licensed banks classify a non-resident International Company as an enhanced-risk offshore vehicle, and standard onboarding requires a face-to-face compliance interview with at least one director and all authorized signatories, conducted at the bank's Apia branch or exceptionally at a correspondent branch under an accepted banker's introduction arrangement. A remote opening is theoretically possible using certified true copies, apostilled resolutions, and a recorded video interview, but the CBS's supervisory expectation for investment vehicles pushes banks to demand either a physical visit or a full-scope due-diligence certificate produced by a correspondent bank on the directors' home jurisdiction. The pragmatic route is to appoint a SIFA-licensed registered agent in Samoa to attest identities and to interface with the compliance team throughout the onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company status presenting as an offshore shell; suspicion of lack of economic substance and unidentified principals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing from the Samoa Registrar of International Companies (SIFA); registered-agent attestation naming a SIFA-licensed agent; current Memorandum and Articles of Association evidencing a venture-capital management purpose; audited GP financial statements or accountant's compilation report; the Fund Legal Agreement, General Partner deed, investment committee charters, and a written substance statement describing the GP's fund management activities in Samoa and abroad; regulatory status confirmation from SIFA reflecting any financial-services licensing or registration in progress.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and frequent inbound capital-call wires from dispersed jurisdictions with opaque source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: LP subscription register with executed Subscription Agreements and Deeds of Adherence; capital commitment schedules and drawdown notices; the Investor AML/KYC file for each limited partner comprising passport, proof of address, corporate ownership chart, PEP and sanctions screening (UN, EU, UK, US OFAC, APG), and source-of-funds attestation; bank reference letters from the LP's home institutions; completed CBS Report on International Transactions; and a written treasury policy describing the expected wire cadence, counterparty jurisdictions, and investment purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons among investors or GP principals triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Risk-rated PEP file with independent source-of-wealth statement, tax returns or asset valuation documentation, explanations for any adverse media, confirmation of the exact nature of any public office held, external EDD report prepared by a licensed investigator, and a board-level waiver approved by the GP's compliance officer confirming that no improper influence or funds of illicit origin are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment pattern inconsistent with declared venture-capital activity, including round-tripping or unexplained diversions to tax-favored jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fund Limited Partnership Agreement and GP Management Agreement; investment pipeline list with conflict-of-interest disclosures; executed term sheets for portfolio companies; the portfolio's due-diligence memoranda and valuation papers; a projected disbursement schedule matched to capital calls; periodic cash-flow models; and a Treasury Policy Memo expressly prohibiting non-investment counterparties and affirming that all outbound wires will reference underlying investment or expense documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Director or signatory nexus to a high-risk jurisdiction, identity document discrepancies, or absence of clear signing authority
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport copies cross-checked against World-Check and equivalent screening; original or apostilled birth certificates and any change-of-name instruments; notarized board minutes appointing signatories; notarized and legalized powers of attorney authenticated for use in Samoa; criminal record checks from the directors' home jurisdictions; and a SIFA-licensed agent's executed attestation confirming the identity and authority of each signatory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: LP capital calls are settled by SWIFT MT103 from each limited partner to the IC's USD operational account held with a CBS-licensed Authorized Dealer (BSP or ANZ Samoa), with MT202 cover for intermediary banks where required. Every incoming wire must include the IC's exact legal name, a unique drawdown reference number, and a coded narrative tied to the capital-call notice; the receiving bank will require the signed Capital Call Notice, a completed CBS balance-of-payments/exchange-control declaration, and an LP source-of-funds attestation for amounts above the applicable reporting threshold. Funds are swept into a segregated Capital Escrow Account to isolate uncalled commitments from operating liquidity; any WST conversion is executed at prevailing CBS interbank rates and is permissible for non-resident accounts without additional surrender obligations. Same-day availability applies after sanctions and PEP screening, and a pre-advice MT799 message is recommended to accelerate clearing. All MT103 records, investor registers, and drawdown documents must be retained for a minimum of seven years for CBS inspection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements to portfolio companies and service providers route primarily through SWIFT MT103 core wires quoting the portfolio-company identifier and board-approved drawdown authorization; MT202 cover payments apply when the beneficiary bank operates a nested account structure. For equity and convertible-note subscriptions, banks require the LPA valuation memo, the investee's KYC pack, and a board resolution confirming the investment. Commercial letters of credit under UCP600 are available but atypical for venture-stage disbursements; they are used only where a portfolio company requires documentary trade settlement and the issuing bank confirms the LC structure as a permissible outbound rail. Management-fee sweeps and carried-interest distributions to non-resident principals are processed as current-account remittances with the IC's tax-exemption certificate attached and the applicable exchange-control form completed. The IC must maintain a Pre-Approved Disbursement Register so that each wire matches a listed investment, expense, or distribution purpose, thereby minimizing bank hold requests and CBS exception reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST spot transactions executed at CBS interbank rates through licensed Authorized Dealers
Outright USD/WST deliverable forwards with tenors of 1 to 12 months offered by BSP and ANZ Samoa on production of an underlying capital-call or disbursement exposure schedule

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/WST executed through international banks with a Samoan licensed intermediary or via a foreign-account-only treasury structure, subject to CBS reporting of the underlying current-account exposure
Vanilla USD/WST foreign-exchange options selectively provided by correspondent banks where an identifiable investment commitment justifies premium payments
Cross-currency swaps on USD/WST are not permissible domestically given the absence of a WST interest-rate swap market; any hedges must remain in simple forward or NDF form

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual government renewal fee for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) / Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation / license issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late penalty on unpaid fee after 30 days; 1.5% monthly interest thereafter; administrative strike-off from the Register beginning 6 months after non-payment, with reinstatement additional fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual return of the International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 50 plus USD 5 per day; after 90 days, Registrar may refer for compulsory strike-off; significant arrears may trigger a court-ordered restoration without striking-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual compliance declaration under the International Financial Services (Licence) Regulations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) as the licensing body for fund managers / general partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than 31 March following the financial year end (31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of USD 200 per week of non-filing; potential suspension of the venture capital management licence; continued non-compliance leads to written warning, then revocation of licence and disqualification of the GP.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required for (a) any International Company holding a financial services licence from SIFA, including venture capital general partner entities; (b) any IC with annual gross revenue exceeding WST 1 million or total assets exceeding WST 2 million; (c) any IC whose shareholders representing at least 10% of voting rights request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by IASB; if the entity does not trigger audit and is small, SIFA permits a simplified accrual-basis local GAAP framework aligned with the Samoa Companies Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must file beneficial ownership particulars with the Registrar annually within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation; any transfer of shares or change in UBO during the year must be notified to the Registrar within 14 days. A consolidated UBO confirmation is required with the annual return.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Company profits under section 197 of the International Companies Act 1987; general resident-company headline rate is 27% under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2012.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are wholly exempt from Samoa income tax, company tax, capital gains tax, dividend withholding tax, and stamp duty on their profits, distributions, and offshore transactions. No separate tax holiday or preferential deduction regime applies; instead, section 197 of the International Companies Act 1987 grants a statutory zero-rate exemption for as long as the company does not derive Samoa-source income. For comparably taxable Samoan companies, the Income Tax Act 2012 allows deduction of eligible expenditures and a five-year loss carryforward, but this is generally irrelevant to a tax-exempt International Company.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoa income tax return is required for an International Company. The operative annual compliance filing is the International Company Annual Return (Form IC-01), submitted through the Samoan International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-Registry by the licensed registered agent. The Samoan Ministry for Revenue does not issue or assess an IC corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the anniversary date of incorporation, not the financial year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Form IC-01 and the annual government fee must be filed and paid on or before the anniversary date of registration. There is no separate extension regime for tax-exempt International Companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registration number, date of incorporation, and registered agent reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners should state the IC's foreign management address and confirm absence of a Samoan business establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoa registered office address and licensed registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PO Box alone is insufficient; the registered office must be a physical address maintained by the licensed agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, nationality, and identification details of each director and the corporate secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign directors may use their foreign residential address; passports or other government-issued ID should be appended for AML/CFT purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part D — Shareholder and Beneficial Ownership Register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal and beneficial ownership chain, including details of the venture capital fund and ultimate natural-person beneficiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The GP entity holding interests in the Samoa IC must provide full beneficial-ownership details, including trust or fund structure charts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the IC has not carried on business with Samoan residents, has no Samoa-source income, does not hold Samoa land, and has not breached the International Companies Act 1987.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident VC GPs should certify that all capital calls, management fees, carried interest, and investment assets relate exclusively to offshore activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized and issued share capital, paid-up capital, and any notes on distributions or capital reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No income tax computation is required; however, capital call records and distribution records should be consistent with the fund's audited statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment of the annual fee attracts a 10% late penalty for the first month and an additional 10% per month or part thereof thereafter. Continued default enables the Registrar to strike the IC off the register after notice, imposes reinstatement fees plus arrears, and can result in the registered agent being disqualified. False statements made in Form IC-01 attract criminal liability under the International Companies Act 1987 and, where relevant, the Samoa Income Tax Act 2012.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends and other distributions paid by an International Company, by virtue of section 197 of the International Companies Act 1987. The general Samoan statutory withholding tax rate on dividends paid by a taxable resident company to a non-resident is 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because an International Company distribution is already exempt at source, DTA relief is normally not required. For a taxable Samoan company, a non-resident payee must file with the Samoa Ministry for Revenue a form claiming reduced treaty withholding, attach a current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the payee's residence jurisdiction, provide a beneficial-ownership declaration evidencing no pass-through of the income, and obtain explicit approval before the payment date. Until approval is granted, the payer must withhold at the domestic statutory rate. All supporting documents must be retained for at least seven years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Samoa withholding tax on cross-border interest paid to non-residents is 15% and on royalty payments for intellectual property is 15%. However, royalty and interest payments made by an International Company in the course of its exempt offshore business are not subject to Samoan withholding tax. Where a Samoa double taxation agreement applies, treaty rates generally reduce the domestic rate and require a Tax Residency Certificate to be submitted to the withholding agent before the payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No local-file or master-file obligation applies to a tax-exempt International Company because it has no Samoan assessable income. For a taxable Samoan company, contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is triggered when annual related-party cross-border transactions exceed WST 500,000 or when the taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds WST 5,000,000. Tax-exempt ICs still need to maintain transaction records sufficient to demonstrate arm's-length charges for management fees, carried interest allocations, and expense reimbursements if challenged.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not impose separate Economic Substance Regulations comparable to BVI or Cayman Islands rules. Nevertheless, an International Company must maintain a valid registered office and licensed registered agent in Samoa, keep adequate records, and refrain from domestic Samoan business. The exemption under section 197 of the International Companies Act 1987 will be denied or retroactively revoked if the entity is managed and controlled from Samoa, earns Samoa-source income, or is used as a shell to avoid taxes that would otherwise be payable by the underlying fund or its principals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly claiming International Company tax exemption while the entity receives management fees, carried interest, or investment income from Samoan residents; filing false annual returns; or concealing distributions to Samoan beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2012 the tax authority may assess evaded tax at 27%, impose a civil penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded, and initiate criminal prosecution carrying fines up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Assets connected to the evasion are subject to freezing, seizure, and forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the IC is a mere facade for fraud; directors, the general partner, and individual promoters are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of diverted profits and may face travel bans, director disqualification, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Samoa International Company as a letterbox vehicle with no physical office, no staff, no board meetings, and no commercial substance while booking carried interest and management fees through the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may strike the IC off the register, the International Finance Authority may suspend or revoke the licensed agent, and the tax exemption may be disallowed with retrospective effect, causing all profits of the venture capital GP to be taxed at 27%. Public register disclosure of the shell status may also be ordered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow managers are personally liable for liabilities incurred through fraudulent trading; courts can order civil restitution of fees extracted, issue travel bans pending investigation, and impose imprisonment where the deficient substance is part of a deliberate tax evasion scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Non-Compliance by Venture Capital GP
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting capital call wires from unidentified third parties, failing to conduct customer due diligence on fund investors, failing to maintain beneficial ownership records, or failing to report suspicious transactions connected to the GP or fund.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and supporting AML/CFT Rules, the body corporate is liable to fines up to WST 1,000,000, cancellation of the financial services licence, confiscation of proceeds, and public reprimand; individuals knowingly involved face imprisonment up to ten years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and the GP's natural-person signatories may be prosecuted personally, subjected to civil asset confiscation, restricted from international travel, and made personally liable for funds lost to money laundering schemes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC provides investment advice to Samoan residents, manages Samoan-resident capital, conducts domestic banking or fund administration, owns Samoan land, or otherwise carries on business with Samoan residents beyond the narrow exceptions in the International Companies Act 1987.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Companies Act 1987 exemption ceases immediately; the company is treated as a resident taxable company at 27%; unlicensed financial service activity is illegal and subject to fines, licence revocation, winding-up, and voidance of affected contracts. The Ministry for Revenue may assess additional penalties and interest on unreported income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and persons knowingly engaged in the prohibited onshore business cannot rely on limited liability; they are jointly and severally liable for all company debts and third-party losses, and may be subject to civil restitution orders, travel bans, and imprisonment for carrying on unlicensed financial services.
